suggestions.prompt: Make the booking form save each drop-off instead of opening an email, and add a private page where only I can see them, sorted by drop-off day.

instructions:
This project is a website for an independent auto repair shop. Content lives as data at the top of app.js; keep it there when making changes:
- BUSINESS holds the name, phone, email, address, street, license, bays, technicians, makes, rating and timezone, and fills every place they appear. Change contact details there, not in the HTML. When the shop, town or prices change, also update the <title> and meta description in index.html, which are static.
- SERVICES and VEHICLES are the price list. The quick quote, service cards, booking form and work order all read them. Prices are typical ranges, not fixed quotes: keep the wording that the shop confirms the price and the customer approves it before work starts.
- LIGHTS is the warning light guide. Keep the safety advice for red lights (oil pressure, temperature, brakes, a flashing check engine light): stop when safe, do not keep driving, call the shop or a tow.
- HOURS and BOOKING drive the open/closed status and the drop-off days, in BUSINESS.timezone. A booking is a request the shop confirms, not a guaranteed slot, unless a real booking backend is added.
- ENQUIRY is where bookings go: endpoint (a JSON POST) if set, otherwise an email to ENQUIRY.email or BUSINESS.email. Ask the user for their own destination; never leave example.com in a published site.
- The reviews, rating, review count, specials, jobs, license number and photos are placeholders, and SAMPLE_CONTENT = true labels them on the page. Never invent reviews, ratings, certifications (such as ASE), warranties, offers or job details for the user's real shop; ask for real ones, or remove what they do not have. Set SAMPLE_CONTENT to false only once those are the user's own.
- Keep the call and booking buttons easy to reach on a phone, including the bar fixed to the bottom of small screens.

instructions:
This is a four-page website for a coffee shop: index.html (home), menu.html, about.html (our story) and visit.html.
The shop details (name, address, phone, email, time zone, order and map links, form endpoints, roast day), opening hours, parts of the day, menu, beans, amenities, reviews, directions and contact topics are plain data in content.js. Change content there rather than in the markup, and keep each entry's shape: a menu price is a number, or [small, regular] for a drink sold in both cup sizes.
app.js is the page code shared by every page. Headlines and copy are in each page's HTML, and colors and fonts are CSS variables at the top of styles.css.
Every page repeats the same header and footer, so a change to the menu bar, logo or footer must be made on every page. A new page must copy the same <head> (error snippet first, the Puter runtime tag, fonts, styles.css, content.js and app.js) and be linked from the menu bar and footer on every page.

instructions:
This project is a website for a dental practice. Content lives as data at the top of app.js; keep it there when making changes:
- PRACTICE holds the name, dentist, phone, emergency line, email, address, license and time zone, and fills every place they appear. Change contact details there, not in the HTML. When the practice, dentist or treatments change, also update the <title> and meta description in index.html, which are static.
- HOURS drives the open-now line, the hours table and the days the booking form offers, in PRACTICE.timeZone.
- INSURANCE is the list the insurance checker and the booking form read. Each booking REASON names a TEAM member, and the form sends to that person, or to PRACTICE.email when they have no email. Keep this routing when adding reasons or people.

Set SAMPLE_CONTENT to false only once these are the dentist's own.

- The booking form must not collect health details (symptoms, history, medications), which fall under privacy rules like HIPAA. Keep the note asking visitors to leave them out. If asked to save requests or add health questions, store only contact and scheduling details and tell the user they need a compliant intake system for the rest.

instructions:
This project is a website for a trucking company (a truckload carrier). Content lives as data at the top of app.js; keep it there when making changes:
- BUSINESS is the company identity: name, phone, email, address, USDOT and MC numbers, insurance amounts and timezone. It fills every place they appear. Change contact details there, not in the HTML. When the company, base city or lanes change, also update the <title> and meta description in index.html, which are static.
- EQUIPMENT and RATES are the trailers and ballpark prices. The rate request quotes them; its price is labeled a guide, not a quote, and must stay that way unless the user says their rates are fixed. RATES.show = false hides the price.
- CITIES, HOME and LANES are where the company runs. The map, departures board, rate request cities, miles and transit days all read them. Miles are estimated from coordinates unless a lane sets miles.
- DRIVERS drives the pay calculator, perks and the application. Keep the calculator labeled an estimate, not an offer.
- HOURS is when the office is staffed; dispatch is described as 24/7. If the user does not run 24/7 dispatch, change that wording everywhere.
- ENQUIRY is where rate requests and applications go: endpoint (a JSON POST) if set, otherwise an email to ENQUIRY.quotes or ENQUIRY.drivers, falling back to BUSINESS.email. Ask the user for their own destination; never leave example.com in a published site.
- The USDOT and MC numbers, insurance, safety record, stats, reviews and photos are placeholders, and SAMPLE_CONTENT = true labels them on the page and hides the FMCSA lookup link. Never invent authority numbers, insurance, safety ratings, inspection rates, reviews or stats for the user's real company; ask for real ones, or remove what they do not have. Set SAMPLE_CONTENT to false only once those are the user's own.
- Do not describe the company as a broker unless the user says it is one; the copy says it hauls on its own trucks.

description: Make your link play an interactive card inside X posts.

suggestions.label: Set my published address
suggestions.prompt: Point the card tags in index.html at my published address: update twitter:player to it and twitter:image to its /preview.png. My address is:

suggestions.prompt: Use the image I upload as preview.png, the picture X shows before someone presses play, and keep it square.

instructions:
This project is an X (Twitter) Player Card: when the page's link is posted on X, X plays the page itself inside a 480 by 480 card. Whatever the user changes, keep that working:
- Keep every twitter:* meta tag (card, site, title, description, image, player, player:width, player:height) written directly in the <head> of index.html. X does not run JavaScript, so never add or change them from a script.
- twitter:player must be the page's own full https:// address, and twitter:image a full https:// address too; X does not accept relative paths. A new copy's card tags still point at the template's site, not the user's, so after the user publishes, ask for their published address and update every card tag to it.
- When the page or the user's content changes, update twitter:title and twitter:description to match. If the preview image changes, raise the ?v= number on the twitter:image address (?v=2, then ?v=3, and so on).
- X keeps its first copy of a card for each link, so an updated page still shows the old card on X. Every time the user publishes an update, tell them to post the link with a new ?v= number at the end (their address plus ?v=2, then ?v=3, and so on), or X shows the old version.
- The steps, the "Make your own" buttons and the links to the template's page are only the template's placeholder content. When the user puts in their own content, replace them; do not keep links to the template or to Puter AI Builder unless the user asks.
- The page must work inside a 480 by 480 frame: the most important content fits in the first 480 pixels, links open in a new tab (target="_blank"), and the .in-frame scrolling in index.html and styles.css stays in place so the card can scroll.
- Keep the page free of anything that blocks framing, such as an X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors setting.

features.body: The card shows the steps to make your own until you put your own content in it.

pageTitle: X Player Card Template: Put Something Interactive in a Post
pageDescription: Put an app or video inside an X (Twitter) post with this Player Card template, which plays your page in the timeline when you share the link.
ogTagline: Something people can use inside an X post

faq.q: What is an X Player Card?
a: It is a type of link preview on X (formerly Twitter). Instead of a picture and a title, the post shows a box that loads a web page in a frame, so people can play or watch without leaving their feed. X shows it when the linked page has twitter:card set to player and a twitter:player address.

faq.q: Why do I have to add my published address after publishing?
a: X needs full https:// addresses in the card tags, and your copy does not have its own until you publish it. Publish once, then give the builder your address and it points the card tags at it.

faq.q: Why does the card not play on my phone?
a: The X phone apps usually show the preview image with a play button rather than the box itself. Check your post in a desktop browser first, where the card plays inline.

faq.q: I fixed the card but X still shows the old one. What now?
a: X keeps its first copy of a card for each link. Post the link again with something added to the end, like ?v=2, and X reads the page fresh.

faq.q: Can I put an app in a Player Card?
a: X’s rules say Player Cards are for video and audio. A card with an app in it works, but X can turn it into a plain link at any time. Test from a protected account first if you want to see the card before anyone else does.
